hellobye

hellobye is a private chatting website. Your conversations stay between you and the people you trust — no public feeds, no strangers, no noise. Just clean, encrypted, one-to-one and group chats in a space built for privacy.

Questions & Answers
Everything you need to know before you sign in or create an account.
Is HelloBye free to use?

Yes. HelloBye is completely free — there are no paid plans, hidden fees, or premium walls. Every feature, from direct messages to group chats, is available to everyone.

Are my messages private?

Your conversations stay between you and the people you talk to. There are no public feeds or strangers, and you can start an encrypted chatroom for messages only the two of you can read.

How do I create an account?

Select the Create Account tab, choose a username (3–20 letters, numbers or underscores) and a password of at least 6 characters, then confirm it to finish signing up.

Can I use HelloBye on my PC?

Yes. Visit the Get HelloBye for PC page to download the native Windows app. It keeps itself up to date and remembers your login across restarts.

I forgot my password — what now?

Click Reset Password under the Sign In button. Follow the steps to verify your account and set a new password, then sign in again.

Who can see my profile?

Only the people you chat with. You control your display name, avatar, bio and status, and you can hide your last-seen time or block anyone you don't want to hear from.

Encryption Chat Request

@user wants to start an end-to-end encrypted chatroom with you. If you both join, you'll each receive a one-time 24-letter key. Only the two of you will ever be able to read this chatroom.

Your One-Time Encryption Key

This key is shown only once. Copy and save it somewhere safe — you'll need it every time you enter this encrypted chatroom.

••••••••••••••••••••••••
If you lose this key, you will not be able to re-enter the encrypted chatroom. It cannot be recovered.

Enter Encryption Key

Enter the 24-letter key you saved to open the encrypted chatroom with @user.

Reset Encryption Key?

@user wants to reset the end-to-end encryption key for this chatroom. If you accept, a brand-new key will be issued to both of you, the old key will stop working, and all messages encrypted with the old key will be permanently deleted. If you decline, nothing changes.

Delete Encryption Key?

@user wants to delete the end-to-end encryption key for this chatroom. If you accept, the key will be permanently deleted for both of you and all messages encrypted with it will be permanently deleted. If you decline, nothing changes.

Return to Normal DMs?

@user wants to leave the encrypted chatroom and return to normal direct messages. If you both accept, you'll switch back to the normal DM. If you both deny, the encrypted chatroom UI will close.

Skipping the // /api/me call avoids a 401 "Not authenticated" console error that // would otherwise fire on every visit for logged-out users. showAuth(); return; } // We have a session ID — the early head script already hid auth via CSS // (html.has-session). Activate the chat app grid so it becomes visible. ensureLoadingOverlay(); chatApp.classList.add('active'); // Show a loading overlay on the chat area until data loads document.body.classList.add('loading-session'); fetch(API_BASE + '/api/me').then(r => r.json()).then(meData => { if (meData.user) { initChat(meData); } else { // Session invalid — clear everything and show auth localStorage.removeItem('hellobye_sid'); document.cookie = 'hellobye_session=; expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 UTC; path=/;'; document.documentElement.classList.remove('has-session'); showAuth(); } }).catch(() => { // Network error — if we had a SID, keep showing chat (offline mode feel) // otherwise show auth if (!hasSid) { document.documentElement.classList.remove('has-session'); showAuth(); } }).finally(() => { document.body.classList.remove('loading-session'); }); } init();
